content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Create an corner with two 140x140 plates at a 90° angle to each other. The first plate has in its center a cutout of 45x45. All plates are 10mm thick | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Implementation concept – step-by-step, using only the provided functions
------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Define the reference coordinate system  
   • The global origin (0 ,0 ,0) will be placed at the lower-front-left corner of the L-shaped corner part.  
   • All block dimensions will be given as positive extensions along the +X, +Y and +Z axes.

2. Add Plate 1 – the “horizontal” plate  
   • Geometry: 140 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z)  
   • Base-point: (0 ,0 ,0) – so it occupies X 0-140, Y 0-140, Z 0-10.  
   • Because this is the first solid, its subtraction flag must be False.

3. Add Plate 2 – the “vertical” plate set at 90 ° to Plate 1  
   • Geometry: 10 mm (X) × 140 mm (Y) × 140 mm (Z)  
     (Thickness is 10 mm along X; the plate rises 140 mm in Z and runs 140 mm in Y.)  
   • Base-point: (0 ,0 ,0) as well – so it occupies X 0-10, Y 0-140, Z 0-140.  
   • The plate therefore intersects Plate 1 in the volume X 0-10, Y 0-140, Z 0-10, creating a perfectly connected 90 ° corner.  
   • Subtraction flag: False (it is an added solid).

4. Create the central cut-out in Plate 1  
   • Required aperture: 45 mm × 45 mm, through the full 10 mm thickness of Plate 1.  
   • Center position in Plate 1’s face is at (70 ,70) in the XY-plane.  
     − Block base-point = (70 − 22.5, 70 − 22.5, 0) = (47.5 , 47.5 , 0).  
     − Block size   = 45 mm (X) × 45 mm (Y) × 10 mm (Z).  
   • Subtraction flag: True, so this volume is removed.

5. Combine the three blocks in a single call to functions.block  
   • Pass each parameter as an array with three entries (one per block).  
   • Ensure that the first entry in the subtraction array is False.

6. Finish the geometry with functions.finished (allFunctionsCalled = true) after the block call.

The next message can now be a ready-to-run function-call payload that follows exactly the steps above.

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
